title: Chan 2004 protocol-publication audit: published trials can still hide measured outcomes
summary: A within-study audit-pair record: protocols versus journal articles reveal that publication alone does not expose all measured outcomes, especially when statistical significance affects reporting completeness.

status_history.note: Promoted in rev0009 as a reporting-bias / file-drawer audit record.

place.scope: randomized trial protocols and publications in a regional ethics-committee cohort

claims.claim: Chan et al. 2004 compared trial protocols with published articles for 102 randomized trials and 122 publications, directly testing within-study outcome-reporting bias.
what_would_change_status: Protocol/publication extraction corrections change trial/article counts.

handling_notes: Reporting-bias records should be framed as evidence-system audits, not blame surfaces.
Nonpublication, delayed publication, or outcome switching can arise from many causes; only source-backed explanations should be stated.
Do not use a single audit record as a universal estimate for all fields, journals, sponsors, or time periods.
